name: Replit
summary: Browser-based coding environment with instant deploys and an AI agent. Billing is effort-based: each plan includes monthly credits that the Agent draws down at a rate you do not set, the credits expire monthly, and a complex agent session burns them fast, which makes production costs hard to budget.
best_for: developers, learners and tinkerers who want a zero-setup, browser-based coding environment with AI assistance
skip_if: you need a stable, cost-predictable production environment — the expiring-credit model makes AI-heavy usage hard to budget
honest_knock: The subscription price is fixed; the paid Agent work is not. Everyday building can run in Free Mode at no extra cost, within an allowance that resets every five hours on Core and Pro and a daily cap on Starter, but anything past it is billed by effort, and only Pro's unused credits roll over. Replit asks before each paid request starts and lets you set a budget, so set one before long sessions. Great for learning and prototyping; watch the meter for production work.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-26 on replit.com/pricing and docs.replit.com/billing/plans/starter-plan) The pricing page now lists Core, Pro and Enterprise. The free Starter plan is no longer shown there but still exists in Replit's documentation: daily Agent credits up to a monthly cap, Free Mode with a daily cap (the experience Replit used to call Lite build), no Full build (that needs Core or Pro), one published app that goes down after 30 days, and a 'Made with Replit' badge on it. Core is $20/month, or $18/month billed annually, and includes $20 towards the most powerful models, up to 30 hours of chat and up to 60 projects on Free Mode, Plan mode and unlimited workspaces. Pro starts at $100/month, or $90/month billed annually, with $100 of credits, 10 parallel agents, up to 15 collaborators, up to 50 viewers and a 28-day database recovery window (point-in-time restore; seven days is the standard window); a dropdown raises Pro to $225, $440, $850 or $2,050 a month ($215, $425, $825 or $2,000 billed annually) for more credits. Enterprise is quote-only. The number to watch is not the seat but the credits: Free Mode covers everyday Agent work at no extra cost within an allowance, and paid requests are priced by effort, so the monthly credit allowance is a starting balance rather than a budget. Replit asks before each paid request starts and lets you set a budget.

structured_checks.task: Code can be exported (GitHub or zip) and data downloaded
structured_checks.detail: run on 26 September 2026: the project zip export held the full source and its git history, but no database contents. Outside Replit it installed and built with pnpm 10 (pnpm 12 refused) once PORT and BASE_PATH were set, and ran against our own empty Postgres: schema created, a booking accepted and counted, admin login refused with a wrong password. The admin password the agent chose is stored as a plain value in the project's .replit file and is in the git history, so it travels with every export.
structured_checks.applies_to: the product as it was on run_date, on the plan stated; a later version inherits nothing

sessions.what: On 26 September 2026 we built the same class-booking web app in Lovable, Replit and Emergent from one identical prompt, each on its free plan, and checked every result against 18 tests we wrote down before the first build. We changed no code: the builder only got our prompt and, where a test failed, a repair prompt in fixed words. Replit ran on a new Starter account, separate from the paid account Daan uses for his own project.
findings: The Agent built a separate API and web app on PostgreSQL in 8 minutes of work by its own count, ran its own functional test and reported everything as passing. It did not publish by itself: publishing is a manual click, and on Starter the deployment is labelled temporary and will expire.

Its own test booked one person at a time. When we sent ten bookings for an empty eight-spot class at the same moment, all ten were accepted, after which the class list returned an error and the public page showed 'No classes on the calendar yet.' until two bookings were cancelled.

Given that exact description, the Agent added a database lock per class in two minutes; the same ten simultaneous bookings then gave exactly eight. The same repair stopped it accepting a name made only of spaces.

On Starter the usage page is closed ('You must have an active subscription to view your own usage'), so you cannot see what a request cost, and the daily allowance was gone after the build and one repair.
sessions.not_tested: One run on one day, on the free plan's agent mode; Core may behave differently. Not a security audit or a load test. The code export was run from the project zip: it built and ran outside Replit on our own database, and carried the admin password in plain text.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
